Subject: Smart fanout & tool-calling playbook — post-demo recap + next actions

Hi Ayla / Tom — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum while you validate internally.

Key outcomes (summary):
- You want the assistant to run three lookups in parallel for each user query: internal KB search (company docs), vector semantic search over product transcripts (embeddings + reranker), and a live web-checker that pulls external pricing pages.
- Preferred output: a structured response that includes a ranked list of candidate sources, confidence scores, and a recommended action (e.g., escalate to human, return short answer, attach doc link).
- Security ask: FinRex needs mTLS for data-plane calls and a short checklist for vendor audit (SOC2 evidence + data retention details).

Technical approach we propose (high-level):
1) Tool defs: define lightweight, typed tool contracts (JSON Schema) for each tool: kb_search, vec_search, web_checker, and a reranker that accepts candidate ids + embeddings. Return format: {"candidates":[], "scores":[], "meta":{}} and an optional "partial" flag for timeouts.
2) Parallel invocation: Redwood runtime will fan out to three tool endpoints concurrently, stream partial responses, and run the reranker as soon as candidates arrive. Where applicable we’ll use model-side scoring + a lightweight CPU reranker for deterministic business rules.
3) Error handling & fallbacks: per-call deadline (300ms default), if one tool times out return partial results and mark tool as degraded in response meta; fallback policy allows a low-cost model-only answer when all tools fail.
4) Auth & SDK: recommend mTLS for tool endpoints; SDK samples in Node/Python (we'll provide) show how to register tool endpoints and sign requests to the private control plane.

Attachments: example-tool-defs.yaml (sample tool contracts) and auth-checklist.pdf (audit entries you asked for).

Next steps (proposed):
- FinRex: confirm the three tool endpoints and whether the web_checker can accept a short proxy token (Ayla).
- Redwood: produce a short PoC plan (3 days) and a sandbox account with configured tool hooks + example SDK snippets (Irene/Karthik).
- Security: share the SOC2 + retention notes and an mTLS onboarding checklist (Ben).

Can you confirm the endpoints and whether a 300ms tool deadline is OK for your UX? If so we’ll schedule a 30-min technical handoff next week to wire up the sandbox.

Thanks —
Irene

Looping in a few implementation specifics we discussed internally — technotes for the PoC handoff: 

1) Tool definition format (concrete):
- Each tool = microservice with a small JSON contract. Example fields: name, input_schema (JSON Schema URL), output_schema (JSON Schema URL), timeout_ms, auth_type (mTLS|api_key), allowed_origins. We will prototype with YAML + JSON Schema in the sandbox.

2) Parallelism & orchestration:
- Redwood runtime will use async fanout with backpressure and streaming: tokens returned from model are buffered, and tool responses can be merged into the stream as they arrive. For the PoC we’ll use an eager merging strategy: first-rank candidates from any tool are injected into the response stream; final reranker runs at the 2nd phase to re-rank before the final message.

3) Reranker & embeddings:
- Use your existing embeddings vector store (you mentioned Pinecone) — we’ll accept candidate ids + dense vectors, run a lightweight cross-encoder reranker (small L2 model on CPU) to get stable ordering. If vector store cannot return embeddings with scores we’ll fetch vectors and compute cosine locally in the sandbox.

4) Error handling patterns:
- Per tool: 3 retries with exponential backoff but bounded to not exceed total user deadline.
- Partial payloads: tools can return a "partial" boolean + truncated candidates list. Runtime will annotate the response meta so UX can display "incomplete".
- Fallbacks: default fallback = model-only summary generated from cached KB docs (fast, lower confidence). Secondary fallback = safe answer template with links to contact support.

5) Auth & onboarding:
- mTLS is preferred for the data plane. For early PoC we can accept short-lived API keys behind the FinRex proxy. We’ll include steps for rotating keys and an automated health-check endpoint.

6) Observability:
- We’ll emit per-tool latency metrics, timeout counts, and per-request model/reranker scores to the console so your SRE can validate end-to-end.

Irene/Vanessa: I can draft the concrete tool YAMLs by Monday night and push to the shared Drive.
